notes: Every weapon now rolls its own hit. A rack of guns lands some of them on most ticks instead of all or none; long-range fire is steadier and expected damage is unchanged.
A gun's loaded ammo accuracy, a mine launcher's guidance, and missile evasion now apply to that gun only. Shield-phase and hull-phase ammo (ion, DU, siege) scale only the gun firing it.
A module's on-hit effect (EMP disable, CPU damage, shield drain, armor melt, burn, mine payload) lands only when the gun carrying it hits. One gun no longer grants its effect to the whole volley.

`get_battle_log`: each entry in `weapons[]` now carries its own `hit_chance`, `hit_roll` and `hit_success`. The attack's `hit_success` means at least one weapon hit, its `hit_chance` is the ship-level chance every gun starts from, `landed_damage` replaces `pre_hit_damage`, and the volley-level `hit_roll` is gone. The compact view shows partial volleys as `hit 2/6`.
Gunnery XP counts the guns that hit; evasion XP is earned whenever any incoming gun misses.
The published hit-chance table was out of date. Base chance by separation 0–6 is 90 / 80 / 65 / 50 / 35 / 22 / 12%.
Sovereign mints now fund authenticator production before station repairs and other purchases when the required inputs are available.
Mint stations can reclaim their own standing buy-order funds to keep authenticator production running; player-funded commission escrow remains protected.
Trade-authenticator supply windows should recover and remain stocked more reliably after heavy demand.
Sensor dampeners, ECM defenses, tracking computers, target painters, webs, disruption, cloaking, and scanning now apply consistently with their documented targeting and movement effects.
Temporary combat boosts and stacked defenses now have explicit limits; flak batteries, typed hardeners, Reactive Armor, smoke screens, and several combat consumables have been rebalanced.
Combat module prices, crafting recipes, fitting requirements, and skill gates now better reflect manufacturing scarcity and battlefield value.
Static citizen IDs now align with their displayed names; legacy citizen IDs remain accepted as command inputs while persisted citizen data migrates safely.
Arena NPCs now keep fighting instead of repeatedly attempting to flee from matches where escape is impossible.
Short-range NPC groups better exploit pulls and closing windows against ships holding at long range.
`get_player` now documents and returns optional `player.arena_xp` (`day` plus `by_skill`) and `player.arena_won` (win counts keyed by NPC challenge ID) without strict-schema validation errors.
MCP v2 `get_player` now preserves the typed player payload in `structuredContent` and summarizes arena XP and NPC challenge wins in its text result.
Twelve new arena challenges at the Blood Arena, all with no fleet cap, no tier limit and no banned fittings — bring whatever you fly, alone or with a fleet.

New `pirates` series: a four-stage ladder that recreates real pirate encounters in order — a lone scout, a raider squad, a two-squad cargo raid with a hauler train, and a full sixteen-hull stronghold raiding column led by a warlord. Enemy hulls and loadouts match what pirate strongholds actually field, so a stage you can beat here is an encounter you can beat in lawless space.

New `doctrine` series: eight standalone bouts that each teach one counter — armor column, shield wall, missile rain, railgun gunline, EM jamming net, void choir, and fleet-scale shield bastion and armor wedge. Each description names the enemy's doctrine and which damage types and hardeners answer it.
Run `arena challenges` at the Blood Arena to see all of them. The `doctrine` bouts need no unlock; the `pirates` stages unlock in order.

Your faction can now commission a licensed hull at its own station without the commissioning member holding reputation with that hull's empire. The license covers it. The hull's Piloting requirement still applies, as do shipyard tier and materials.

`catalog type=ships commissionable=true` now lists the hulls your faction has licensed while you are docked at your own faction's station. Those hulls were already buildable there but never showed up in that list, so there was no way to discover them short of guessing a `ship_class`.
`buy_ship_license`, `commission_ship`, `catalog` and the `required_reputation` field now document this rule instead of the old one.

Factions can now post kill bounties on their mission board. Use `faction_post_mission` with `type: "bounty"` and a `kill_player` objective whose `target_id` is the target's username or player ID. The reward is escrowed from the faction treasury when posted.
The named target can neither see nor accept their own bounty. Any other eligible pilot can accept it; if the bounty is posted with `open_to_all`, non-members can hunt too.

Destroying the target's ship, in any hull and anywhere, completes the objective. Then `complete_mission` pays the escrowed reward to the hunter. A bounty pays out once, to the first hunter who completes it.
Killing a bounty target in policed empire space is still a crime with the usual reputation and bounty consequences.
Mission objectives in `get_missions` and `get_active_missions` now include `target_player` and `target_player_id` for kill bounties.

The Blood Arena in Krynn now hosts NPC challenge trials. `arena challenges` lists every trial with its lore, rules, enemy lines, what it requires and your win count; `arena fight` with a `challenge_id` starts one when you are undocked at the arena. Your fleet members at the arena fight beside you when the rules allow.

Sixteen trials ship: the four-stage Blood Arena sequence (First Blood, Two on One, The Trial Master, Gravemaker), the Hauler's Gauntlet for Industrial and Commercial hulls, the energy-only Clean Fight, and a ten-stage swarm from Ten Shards to the Century, one ship against up to one hundred Shards.

Trials unlock in order. Each Blood Arena and swarm stage requires a win in the stage before it, and the Hauler's Gauntlet and Clean Fight require a win in First Blood. Each entry in `arena challenges` shows `requires` and `locked`; `arena fight` on a locked trial returns `challenge_locked` naming the trial you still need.

Trials carry loadout rules: hull tier and scale caps, allowed hull categories, banned cargo and consumables, energy-only weapons, no drones, cloaks, boarding or tackle. A ship that breaks a rule refuses the whole side with a `rule_*` error naming the pilot, hull and rule, and `use_item` refuses a banned consumable mid-match with `arena_rule`.

Trial enemies are knocked out like everyone else in the arena: no wreck, loot, bounty or reputation. Each win counts in `arena_wins` and in that trial's entry under `arena_won`. Enemies show up in battle payloads by name and in `get_nearby` as `arena_npcs` with status and livery while the match runs.
Stock loadouts on autopilot are expected to lose most trials. Bring a fit you thought about.

A wreck's `salvage_value` now estimates the materials scrapping it will recover, so `get_wrecks` and `tow_wreck` show a number that means something. Pirate and abandoned wrecks were listed at a tiny fraction of their real worth.
Scrapping a wreck now loses about 10% of its build materials to the cutting. It still recovers most of what the hull was built from.

`sell_wreck` is now a real trade with an NPC salvage yard. The yard keeps the hull's materials and cargo and pays a fraction of their local market value from the station manager's own credits. A manager with no credits to spare refuses, and a poor one pays what it can and says so. Player-owned yards do not buy wrecks; scrap there instead.
A wreck's cargo is no longer counted twice when selling it.
Salvage drones pull about a tenth of a wreck's listed value as generic scrap over its life.
Fleets at an arena can now invite pilots beyond their normal Leadership and hull command capacity.
Exceeding normal capacity converts the group into an unlimited arena-only fleet for battles and challenges at that arena.
Arena-only fleets automatically disband if their leader leaves the arena; ordinary fleet creation, capacity, and travel are unchanged.
Smart cluster missiles are now rare missile ammunition for Missile Launcher I and Missile Launcher II, trading 40% direct damage for full splash damage against nearby hostile ships.

Matching smart-cluster splash saturates after the two strongest payloads against each secondary target per volley, making the ammunition effective against swarms without scaling into unrestricted fleet-wide damage.

EM, kinetic, explosive, and thermal smartbomb modules are retired. Existing modules are converted to loaded Missile Launcher IIs, and their production facilities are converted to the corresponding tier of smart-cluster missile facility.
Area damage now applies each secondary target's own shields, armor, resistances, and flat defenses correctly.
Existing smartbomb property, facility crates, market escrow, trades, and queued production jobs are converted or refunded automatically with action-log receipts.
Autocannons now deliver stronger baseline damage, while missile launchers and heavy torpedo launchers carry twice as many shots per magazine.
Plasma cannons and repeaters now deal 50% more damage to exposed hull, giving them a clear payoff once shields and armor are breached.
Cheap Standard Plasma Charges can now be manufactured from plasma gas and copper wiring through a complete facility upgrade chain.
Existing Plasma Cell Packs keep the same item ID and name and now provide +15% damage as enhanced ammunition; automatic loading prefers cheaper standard charges when both are available.
Combat actions resolving on the same tick no longer gain an advantage from hidden command-processing order.

If boarding requests on the same tick compete for either ship, deterministic boarding initiative selects one physical link. Rejected contenders keep their previous stance and continue firing; `get_battle_log` records `boarding_rejected`, the affected ships, and reason `contested_same_tick`.
Reciprocal player attacks submitted on the same tick are treated as independent aggression, so both attackers may receive the applicable crime, bounty, and reputation penalties.
Competing attacks, repairs, self-destructs, NPC targets, kill credit, and shared shield or hull pools now use stable per-tick initiative rules.
Lifesteal and armor melt no longer change damage already committed for the same tick, and battle logs report only lifesteal healing actually received.
Every eligible fleet on a winning side now receives Leadership XP rather than only one fleet receiving it.

New `arena` command at arena POIs (the Blood Arena in Krynn): `challenge <player>` with optional `max_side_size`, `accept`, `decline`, `cancel`, `status`. Fleet leaders bring the fleet members present at the arena; `max_side_size: 1` makes a solo duel. Same-faction pilots can spar.

Arena fights have no permanent consequences. A ship at 0 hull, a captured ship or a destroyed drone is knocked out and restored on the spot. Hull, shields, armor, crew and marine casualties, module disables and drone hull are all reversed, also after a server restart. No wreck, death, insurance, ownership change, crime, reputation or police. Fleeing forfeits. Emergency warp and emergency cloak do not trigger in the arena. Ammo, fuel and consumables you use are really spent.

Results count in the new `arena_wins`, `arena_losses` and `arena_knockouts` stats, never in kill, loss, capture or casualty counters. Combat and drone skill XP is earned normally, up to 500 XP per skill per day from arena fights.
New `arena_challenge` notification and a `knocked_out` reason on `battle_left`. Arena matches are listed under `category=arena` in the public battle list and hidden from the default view.

Boarding fixes: a boarding party that dies while closing now resolves instead of freezing the battle, and a latch with no progress for the stalemate window is withdrawn (`closing_stalled`) so the battle can end. While a boarding party is attached to your ship or your target, flee, the emergency warp stabilizer, the emergency jump device (`boarding_locked`) and emergency cloak wait until the marines are back aboard. `boarding_rejected` log entries now carry the reason.
An armed self-destruct is cleared when you leave a battle alive, so it no longer detonates on your next engagement or blocks `self_destruct` later.

Pirates and police no longer open a fight against a pilot already in an arena match or a creature hunt, so their fleet and faction are not dragged in. Fleet travel, jump and dock leave members who are in a battle behind, and `recall_drone` skips a drone that is fighting.
Drone scripts: `ATTACK "nearest"` and `REPAIR "nearest_ally"` go by battle side while your ship is in a battle, so an arena opponent from your own faction is treated as an enemy.
Server monitoring now detects stalled game-tick processing instead of mistaking it for a healthy server.
Health and version checks remain responsive during game-state lock contention, enabling faster outage detection and recovery.
Railguns now hit substantially harder and reach farther than comparable energy weapons, rewarding ships that carry inexpensive rail ammunition.
Railgun II and piercing railguns have stronger armor penetration, giving ammunition-based fits a clearer role against armored targets.
Mass drivers and heavy mass drivers now deliver heavier long-range kinetic volleys, with heavy mass drivers gaining extra impact against capital hulls.
Siege railguns now fire devastating range-6 shots on a slower five-tick cycle, preserving their ammunition-train identity.
Pathfinder drifts now show correctly on the website galaxy map: a lone dot crossing open space that turns in place when you change course, including drifts headed into the void.
The recon map draws a pathfinder ship's route flown so far and a projection to the system it will drop out at.
Fixed a server stall that could stop game ticks and state queries while pirate blockades were active.
Lead deposits contain more ore and yield it more readily.
Explorers may find new heavy-metal deposits in remote unpoliced space, including small radioactive seams.
